title: Murakkab matnlarda muallif niyati
goal_uz: Dars oxirida murakkab matnda muallifning maqsadi va munosabatini aniq sifat bilan nomlay olasiz, kamida beshta pozitsiya belgisini topasiz, faktni fikrdan ajratasiz va xulosa savollariga matndan dalil keltirib javob berasiz.

scenes.title: Muallif nima demoqchi?
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda yetti-sakkiz ball darajasidagi argumentli esse yozdik: aniq pozitsiya, kuchli dalil va muvozanatli xulosa. Bugun rolni almashtiramiz: endi siz o‘quvchisiz. Dars oxirida murakkab matnda muallifning maqsadi va munosabatini aniqlay olasiz, faktni fikrdan ajratasiz va imtihondagi xulosa chiqarish savollariga ishonch bilan javob berasiz.
scenes.say: Welcome back. Last time you were the writer. Today you're the reader, and our job is to read between the lines without inventing what isn't there.
scenes.say_uz: Xush kelibsiz. O‘tgan safar siz yozuvchi edingiz. Bugun o‘quvchisiz va vazifamiz satrlar orasini o‘qish, lekin matnda yo‘q narsani o‘ylab topmaslik.

scenes.title: Maqsad va munosabat
board: Attitude = HOW the writer feels about it

examples.t: The writer's purpose is to warn readers about rising debt.
examples.uz: Muallifning maqsadi o‘quvchilarni o‘sib borayotgan qarzdan ogohlantirish.

scenes.say_native: Ikki tushunchani ajratamiz. Maqsad, ya’ni purpose, matn nima uchun yozilganini bildiradi: xabar berish, ishontirish, tanqid qilish, ogohlantirish yoki ko‘ngil ochish. Munosabat, ya’ni attitude, muallifning mavzuga his-tuyg‘usi: ma’qullaydimi, shubha qiladimi, kinoya qiladimi. Bir matnda maqsad xabar berish bo‘lishi, munosabat esa yashirin tanqid bo‘lishi mumkin. Imtihonda ikkalasi alohida so‘raladi.
scenes.say: Purpose is why the text exists. Attitude is how the writer feels about the subject. A report can look neutral while quietly disapproving.
scenes.say_uz: Maqsad matn nima uchun mavjudligi. Munosabat muallifning mavzuga qanday qarashi. Hisobot neytral ko‘rinib, jimgina qoralashi mumkin.

scenes.title: Ochiq va yashirin ma’no

examples.t: The minister's speech was certainly long.

scenes.say_native: Birinchi nuqta: yashirin ma’no va ohang. Explicit ma’no to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri aytiladi, implicit ma’no esa faqat ishora qilinadi. “The minister’s speech was certainly long” gapida muallif nutq yomon demagan, lekin faqat uzunligini tilga olib, mazmuni sayoz bo‘lganini anglatyapti. Muallif imply qiladi, o‘quvchi infer qiladi. Bu ikki fe’lni aralashtirmang.
scenes.say: The minister's speech was certainly long. Nothing negative is stated, yet the message is clear. Writers imply; readers infer.
scenes.say_uz: Vazirning nutqi, shubhasiz, uzun edi. Salbiy gap aytilmagan, ammo xabar aniq. Muallif ishora qiladi, o‘quvchi xulosa chiqaradi.

scenes.title: Ohangni bildiruvchi sifatlar

examples.t: The tone of the review is scathing.
She takes a measured view of the reforms.

scenes.say_native: Ohangni tasvirlash uchun aniq so‘zlar kerak, “positive” yoki “negative” C1 uchun juda umumiy. Sceptical: shubha bilan qaraydigan. Dismissive: mensimaydigan. Scathing: juda keskin tanqid. Measured: vazmin. Ambivalent: ham yoqadi, ham yoqmaydi. Wry: quruq, achchiq hazil. Imtihon variantlarida aynan shu so‘zlar keladi.
scenes.say: A sceptical writer doubts. A dismissive one barely takes the idea seriously. A scathing review tears it apart.
scenes.say_uz: Sceptical muallif shubha qiladi. Dismissive muallif g‘oyani jiddiy ham qabul qilmaydi. Scathing taqriz uni yanchib tashlaydi.

scenes.title: Konnotatsiya: so‘z tanlovi

examples.t: The council's frugal budget...
The council's stingy budget...

scenes.say_native: Ohang ko‘pincha bitta so‘zda yashiringan. Frugal va stingy ikkalasi ham kam pul sarflashni bildiradi, lekin frugal maqtov, stingy esa tanqid. Confident bilan arrogant ham shunday. O‘zbek tilida ham “tejamkor” va “xasis” bir xil ish haqida, lekin munosabat qarama-qarshi. Matnni o‘qiganda o‘zingizdan so‘rang: muallif neytral so‘z tanlashi mumkin edi, nega aynan shu bo‘yoqli so‘zni tanladi?
scenes.say: Frugal and stingy describe the same behaviour. One is praise; the other is an accusation.
scenes.say_uz: Frugal va stingy bir xil xatti-harakatni tasvirlaydi. Biri maqtov, ikkinchisi ayblov.

scenes.title: Kinoya va kamtar ifoda
board: Irony: say the opposite of what you mean
Litotes: not without its problems = many problems

examples.t: The plan is not without its problems.

scenes.say_native: Britan muallifi tanqidni ko‘pincha yumshoq beradi. Understatement: “not entirely convincing” aslida “ishonarsiz” degani. Litotes, ya’ni inkorni inkor qilish: “not without its problems” degani muammolar ko‘p. Kinoyada esa teskarisi aytiladi. O‘zbek tilida biz tanqidni ochiqroq aytamiz, shuning uchun bunday iboralar ko‘pincha neytral deb noto‘g‘ri o‘qiladi.
scenes.say: Not entirely convincing usually means unconvincing. And not without its problems means plenty of problems.
scenes.say_uz: Not entirely convincing odatda ishonarsiz degani. Not without its problems esa muammolar ko‘p degani.

scenes.title: O‘zbek tili bilan qiyos
board: English: word choice, hedges, irony → tone
Look at vocabulary, not grammar endings
afsuski = regrettably · go‘yoki = ostensibly · aftidan = apparently

examples.t: Oh, so the project is finished, is it?

scenes.say_native: O‘zbek tilida munosabatni ko‘pincha yuklamalar orqali bildiramiz: “bilasiz-ku”, “keldi-da”, “shu ham ishmi”. Inglizchada bunday kichik qo‘shimchalar deyarli yo‘q, munosabat so‘z tanlovi, ehtiyotkorlik iboralari va kinoya orqali beriladi. Shuning uchun ingliz matnida ohangni grammatikadan emas, leksikadan qidiring: sifatlar, ravishlar, fe’llar va kutilmagan qiyoslar.
scenes.say: In English, tone rarely lives in grammar endings. It lives in vocabulary: the words a neutral writer would not have chosen.
scenes.say_uz: Ingliz tilida ohang kamdan-kam grammatik qo‘shimchalarda bo‘ladi. U leksikada: neytral muallif tanlamagan so‘zlarda.

scenes.title: Mavzu bilan ohangni aralashtirish
board: Text about a tragedy ≠ tragic tone
✗ The tone is sad because it is about poverty.
scenes.say_native: Keng tarqalgan xato: mavzuni ohang deb o‘ylash. Qashshoqlik haqidagi matn qayg‘uli bo‘lishi shart emas: u g‘azabli, tahliliy yoki hatto kinoyali bo‘lishi mumkin. Ohangni isbotlash uchun matndan aniq so‘zlarni ko‘rsating, masalan “shameful” yoki “entirely avoidable”. Ikkinchi xato: kinoyani to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri o‘qish. Agar maqtov kontekstga mos kelmasa, kinoya bo‘lishi mumkin.
scenes.say: A text about poverty isn't automatically sad. If the writer says shameful and avoidable, the tone is angry.
scenes.say_uz: Qashshoqlik haqidagi matn avtomatik qayg‘uli emas. Muallif uyatli va oldini olsa bo‘ladigan desa, ohang g‘azabli.

scenes.title: Mashq: ohangni aniqlang
board: 1 The new app is, admittedly, very pretty.
2 Another brilliant idea from head office: longer meetings.
3 The proposal has strengths, though costs remain unclear.
scenes.say_native: Endi siz. Doskadagi uchta gapning har biri uchun ohangni tanlang: ironic, measured yoki faintly dismissive. Har bir javobni matndagi bitta so‘z bilan asoslashga harakat qiling. Esda tuting, ohangni mavzu emas, so‘z tanlovi ko‘rsatadi. Pauza qiling va o‘ylab ko‘ring.
scenes.say: Your turn. For each sentence, choose the tone: ironic, measured or faintly dismissive. Then find the one word that proves it. Pause now.
scenes.say_uz: Navbat sizda. Har bir gap uchun ohangni tanlang: kinoyali, vazmin yoki biroz mensimaydigan. Keyin buni isbotlaydigan bitta so‘zni toping. Hozir pauza qiling.

scenes.title: Javoblar: ohang
scenes.say_native: Birinchi gap biroz mensimaydigan: admittedly “tan olish kerak” degani, keyin faqat tashqi ko‘rinish maqtaladi, demak qolgani yaxshi emas. Ikkinchisi kinoyali: “brilliant idea” va “longer meetings” bir-biriga mos emas. Uchinchisi vazmin: kuchli tomonlar tan olinadi, “though” bilan esa ehtiyotkor shubha qo‘shiladi.
scenes.say: One is faintly dismissive. Two is ironic: nobody sincerely calls longer meetings brilliant. Three is measured.
scenes.say_uz: Birinchisi biroz mensimaydigan. Ikkinchisi kinoyali: hech kim uzun yig‘ilishni chin dildan ajoyib demaydi. Uchinchisi vazmin.

scenes.title: Pozitsiya belgilari
board: They comment on the whole sentence

examples.t: Predictably, the committee rejected the plan.
The scheme is ostensibly about safety.

scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi nuqta: muallif pozitsiyasining belgilari. Bular butun gapga baho beradigan ravishlar. Predictably: kutilganidek, muallif hayron emas va biroz norozi. Ostensibly: go‘yoki, rasmiy sabab boshqa, haqiqiysi boshqa. Regrettably: afsuski. Arguably: aytish mumkinki. Surely gap boshida esa ko‘pincha ishontirishga urinish.
scenes.say: Predictably, the committee rejected the plan. One adverb tells you the writer saw it coming and isn't impressed.
scenes.say_uz: Kutilganidek, qo‘mita rejani rad etdi. Bitta ravish muallif buni oldindan bilganini va mamnun emasligini aytadi.

scenes.title: Ehtiyotkorlik iboralari (hedges)
board: Hedges: may · appears to · tends to · to some extent
Boosters: clearly · undoubtedly · there is no question that

examples.t: The data appear to suggest a link.
There is no question that the policy failed.

scenes.say_native: Hedge, ya’ni ehtiyotkorlik vositasi, muallifning ishonch darajasini ko‘rsatadi: may, appears to, tends to, to some extent. Akademik matnda bu hurmatli uslub. Uning aksi booster: clearly, undoubtedly, there is no question that, ya’ni qat’iy ishonch. Tanqidiy o‘qing: ba’zan clearly aynan dalil yo‘q joyda ishlatiladi. Hedge juda ko‘p bo‘lsa esa, muallif xulosasiga ishonmayotgan bo‘lishi mumkin.
scenes.say: The data appear to suggest a link. Hedges signal caution. Their opposite, words like clearly or undoubtedly, signal commitment.
scenes.say_uz: Ma’lumotlar bog‘liqlikka ishora qilayotganga o‘xshaydi. Hedge ehtiyotkorlikni bildiradi. Uning aksi, clearly yoki undoubtedly, qat’iylikni bildiradi.

scenes.title: Iqtibos fe’llari munosabat bildiradi

examples.t: The company claims the product is safe.
examples.uz: Kompaniya mahsulot xavfsiz deb da’vo qiladi.

examples.t: The study demonstrates a clear effect.

scenes.say_native: Muallif boshqalarning fikrini qaysi fe’l bilan keltirishi ko‘p narsa aytadi. Says va states neytral. Claims, alleges, insists masofa saqlaydi: muallif to‘liq ishonmaydi. Demonstrates, shows, points out esa rozilik. Concedes noiloj tan olish. O‘zbekchada “aytdi”, “da’vo qildi”, “isbotladi” farqi xuddi shunday.
scenes.say: The company says it is safe. The company claims it is safe. The study demonstrates it is safe. Three different attitudes.
scenes.say_uz: Kompaniya xavfsiz deydi. Kompaniya xavfsiz deb da’vo qiladi. Tadqiqot xavfsizligini isbotlaydi. Uch xil munosabat.

scenes.title: So-called, supposedly va qo‘shtirnoq

examples.t: The so-called experts got it wrong again.

scenes.say_native: Yana bir kuchli belgi: so-called, supposedly va qo‘shtirnoq. “The so-called experts”: ularni ekspert deyishadi, lekin muallif rozi emas. Supposedly independent: go‘yoki mustaqil. Bitta so‘z qo‘shtirnoqda bo‘lsa, bu ko‘pincha “ular shunday ataydi, men emas” degani. O‘zbekchadagi “go‘yoki” shunga yaqin.
scenes.say: The so-called experts got it wrong again. The supposedly independent report was funded by the industry.
scenes.say_uz: Ekspert deb ataluvchilar yana adashdi. Go‘yoki mustaqil hisobotni sanoatning o‘zi moliyalashtirgan.

scenes.title: Claims va admittedly xatolari
scenes.say_native: Ikki tipik xato. Birinchisi: claims so‘zini neytral deb o‘qish. Ko‘p o‘quvchilar “kompaniya aytdi” deb tarjima qiladi va muallifning shubhasini sezmaydi. Ikkinchisi: admittedly so‘zini “albatta” deb tushunish. Aslida admittedly “to‘g‘ri, tan olaman” degani va undan keyin ko‘pincha “but” yoki qarshi fikr keladi. Ya’ni asosiy pozitsiya keyingi gapda.
scenes.say: Claims is not neutral. And admittedly doesn't mean definitely; it means I'll grant you that.
scenes.say_uz: Claims neytral emas. Admittedly esa albatta degani emas, u “mayli, buni tan olaman” degani.

scenes.title: Mashq: muallif pozitsiyasi
board: 1 The minister insists the figures are accurate.
2 Admittedly, the scheme is cheap. But...
3 The research convincingly shows a link.
Does the writer agree, doubt or concede?
scenes.say_native: Endi pozitsiya belgilarini o‘zingiz toping. Har bir gapda muallif rozimi, shubha qilyaptimi yoki biror narsani tan olyaptimi? Belgi bo‘lgan so‘zning tagiga chizing. Iqtibos fe’llariga alohida e’tibor bering. Uchinchi gapda ikkita belgi bor, ikkalasini toping. Pauza qiling.
scenes.say: In each sentence, does the writer agree, doubt or concede? Underline the marker. Sentence three contains two markers; find both. Pause now.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir gapda muallif rozimi, shubha qilyaptimi yoki tan olyaptimi? Belgining tagiga chizing. Uchinchi gapda ikkita belgi bor, ikkalasini toping. Hozir pauza qiling.

scenes.title: Javoblar: pozitsiya
scenes.say_native: Birinchi gapda insists shubhani bildiradi: vazir qat’iy turib oladi, lekin muallif bunga ishonmaydi, aks holda “shows” yoki “confirms” derdi. Ikkinchisida muallif arzonlikni tan oladi, ammo “but” dan keyin asl tanqid keladi. Uchinchisida ikkita belgi: convincingly ravishi va shows fe’li, ikkalasi ham rozilik. Ko‘ryapsizmi, bitta so‘z pozitsiyani butunlay o‘zgartiradi.
scenes.say: One: doubt, through insists. Two: a concession, then but. Three: agreement, through convincingly and shows.
scenes.say_uz: Birinchi: shubha, insists orqali. Ikkinchi: tan olish, keyin but. Uchinchi: rozilik, convincingly va shows orqali.

scenes.title: Fakt va fikr
board: Fact = can be checked (dates, numbers, events)

examples.t: The bridge opened in 2019.
The bridge is an eyesore.

scenes.say_native: Uchinchi nuqta: fakt va fikr. Fakt tekshirib ko‘rish mumkin bo‘lgan ma’lumot: sana, raqam, voqea. Fikr esa baho, unga boshqa odam asosli ravishda qarshi chiqishi mumkin. Oddiy test: aqlli odam bunga rozi bo‘lmasligi mumkinmi? Agar ha, bu fikr. “Ko‘prik 2019-yilda ochilgan” fakt. “Ko‘prik ko‘zni xira qiladi” fikr. Fakt noto‘g‘ri bo‘lishi ham mumkin, lekin u baribir tekshiriladigan turdagi gap.
scenes.say: The bridge opened in 2019: that can be checked. The bridge is an eyesore: that can be argued with.
scenes.say_uz: Ko‘prik 2019-yilda ochilgan: buni tekshirish mumkin. Ko‘prik ko‘zni xira qiladi: bunga qarshi chiqish mumkin.

scenes.title: Fikrni bildiruvchi til

examples.t: The council should never have approved it.
examples.uz: Kengash buni hech qachon tasdiqlamasligi kerak edi.

examples.t: It was the worst decision in decades.
examples.uz: Bu o‘n yilliklardagi eng yomon qaror edi.

scenes.say_native: Fikrni tanib olishga yordam beradigan belgilar bor. Baholovchi sifatlar: disastrous, admirable, misguided. Modal fe’llar: should, ought to, must, ayniqsa o‘tmish haqida: should have done. Orttirma darajalar: the best, the worst, far more effective. Bunday so‘z bor gap deyarli har doim fikr. Lekin bitta gapda fakt va fikr aralash bo‘lishi mumkin, shuning uchun gapni qismlarga ajrating.
scenes.say: The council should never have approved it. It was the worst decision in decades. Both are opinions.
scenes.say_uz: Kengash buni hech qachon tasdiqlamasligi kerak edi. Bu o‘n yilliklardagi eng yomon qaror edi. Ikkalasi ham fikr.

scenes.title: Fakt kiyimidagi fikr
board: Everyone knows that... · It is a fact that...

examples.t: It is a fact that remote work kills creativity.
examples.uz: Masofaviy ish ijodkorlikni o‘ldirishi fakt. (aslida fikr)

scenes.say_native: Murakkab matnlarda fikr ko‘pincha fakt kiyimida keladi. “Everyone knows that”, “It is a fact that”, “Experts agree” iboralari dalil o‘rniga ishlatiladi. “Remote work kills creativity” esa tekshirib bo‘lmaydigan baho. Gapning boshlanishiga emas, mazmuniga qarang. O‘zbek publitsistikasidagi “hammaga ma’lumki” ham shu vazifani bajaradi.
scenes.say: It is a fact that remote work kills creativity. The frame says fact; the content says opinion.
scenes.say_uz: Masofaviy ish ijodkorlikni o‘ldirishi fakt. Ramka fakt deydi, mazmun esa fikr deydi.

scenes.title: Tanlash va raqamlar ramkasi
board: only 40% (= too few) vs as many as 40% (= a lot)
What is left out is also a choice
Facts can be arranged to persuade

examples.t: Only 40% of students passed.
As many as 40% of students passed.

scenes.say_native: Hatto faktlar ham neytral emas. Bir xil raqam: “only forty per cent” kam degan baho beradi, “as many as forty per cent” esa ko‘p degan baho. Muallif qaysi faktni tanlashi, qaysi birini tashlab ketishi va qaysi tartibda joylashtirishi ham uning pozitsiyasi. Matnda faqat bir tomonning dalillari bo‘lsa, so‘zlar neytral ko‘rinsa ham, maqsad ishontirish.
scenes.say: Only forty per cent passed. As many as forty per cent passed. Same number, opposite attitude.
scenes.say_uz: Atigi qirq foiz o‘tdi. Qirq foizgacha o‘tdi. Raqam bir xil, munosabat qarama-qarshi.

scenes.title: Raqam = neytral degan xato
board: ✗ It has numbers, so it is objective.
✓ Check the framing: only, merely, a staggering
scenes.say_native: Xato: raqam bor ekan, demak matn obyektiv deb o‘ylash. Raqam atrofidagi so‘zlarga qarang: only, merely, a mere, a staggering, a whopping. Bular baho. Shuningdek o‘zingizdan so‘rang: nima bilan solishtirilmoqda? “Crime rose by fifty per cent” qo‘rqinchli eshitiladi, lekin ikkita holatdan uchtaga oshgan bo‘lishi mumkin. Raqamni emas, uning ramkasini o‘qing.
scenes.say: Crime rose by a staggering fifty per cent. That might mean two incidents became three. Compared with what?
scenes.say_uz: Jinoyatchilik hayratlanarli ellik foizga oshdi. Bu ikki holat uchtaga aylangani bo‘lishi mumkin. Nima bilan solishtirilmoqda?

scenes.title: Mashq: F yoki O
board: 1 The museum attracted 2 million visitors last year.
2 Sadly, a mere 2 million people visited.
3 Its new wing is a triumph of design.
4 The wing was designed by a Danish firm.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta gap. Har birini F, ya’ni fact, yoki O, ya’ni opinion deb belgilang. Ehtiyot bo‘ling: bitta gapda fakt va fikr aralash. Qaysi ekanini toping va qaysi so‘zlar fikrni bildirayotganini ayting. Birinchi va ikkinchi gapni bir-biriga solishtiring. Pauza.
scenes.say: Mark each sentence F for fact or O for opinion. Be careful: one sentence mixes both. Find it, and name the words that add the opinion. Pause now.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir gapni F, fakt, yoki O, fikr deb belgilang. Ehtiyot bo‘ling: bitta gap ikkalasini aralashtiradi. Uni toping va fikr qo‘shayotgan so‘zlarni ayting. Hozir pauza qiling.

scenes.title: Javoblar: F yoki O
scenes.say_native: Birinchi va to‘rtinchi gaplar fakt: tashrif buyuruvchilar soni va loyihachi firmani tekshirish mumkin. Uchinchisi sof fikr: “a triumph of design” baho. Ikkinchi gap aralash: ikki million raqami fakt, lekin “sadly” va “a mere” muallif bu raqamni kam deb hisoblashini ko‘rsatadi. Birinchi va ikkinchi gapda raqam bir xil, ammo munosabat butunlay boshqa.
scenes.say: One and four are facts. Three is opinion. Two is mixed: the figure is a fact, but sadly and a mere add a judgement.
scenes.say_uz: Birinchi va to‘rtinchi fakt. Uchinchisi fikr. Ikkinchisi aralash: raqam fakt, lekin sadly va a mere baho qo‘shadi.

scenes.title: Xulosa chiqarish savollari
board: What does the writer imply about...?
The writer's attitude can best be described as...
Answer = not stated, but strongly supported

examples.t: What does the writer suggest about the mayor?
examples.uz: Muallif mer haqida nimaga ishora qiladi?

scenes.say_native: To‘rtinchi nuqta: inference, ya’ni xulosa chiqarish savollari. Ular IELTS, CAE va boshqa imtihonlarda shunday ko‘rinadi: “What does the writer imply”, “It can be inferred that”, “The writer’s attitude can best be described as”. To‘g‘ri javob matnda so‘zma-so‘z yozilmagan, lekin matn uni kuchli qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi. Bu taxmin emas: har bir javobni matndagi aniq dalil bilan isbotlay olishingiz kerak.
scenes.say: Inference questions ask for what is not stated but strongly supported. If you can't point to the words, it isn't the answer.
scenes.say_uz: Xulosa savollari aytilmagan, lekin kuchli asoslangan narsani so‘raydi. So‘zlarni ko‘rsata olmasangiz, bu javob emas.

scenes.title: To‘rt qadamli strategiya
board: 2 Read around: one sentence before and after
4 Eliminate: too extreme / not stated / opposite
scenes.say_native: Strategiya to‘rt qadam. Birinchi: savoldagi kalit so‘zlar bo‘yicha matndan kerakli joyni toping. Ikkinchi: shu gapdan oldingi va keyingi gapni ham o‘qing, chunki pozitsiya ko‘pincha “but” dan keyin keladi. Uchinchi: variantlarga qaramasdan, o‘z so‘zingiz bilan javobni taxmin qiling. To‘rtinchi: noto‘g‘ri variantlarni chiqarib tashlang. Bu tartib sizni chalg‘ituvchi variantlardan himoya qiladi.
scenes.say: Locate, read around, predict in your own words, then eliminate.
scenes.say_uz: Toping, atrofini o‘qing, o‘z so‘zingiz bilan taxmin qiling, keyin chiqarib tashlang.

scenes.title: Chalg‘ituvchi variant turlari
board: Word-match trap: same words, different meaning

examples.t: Text: not entirely convinced → ✗ completely opposed

scenes.say_native: Imtihon tuzuvchilar to‘rt xil tuzoq qo‘yadi. Birinchi: o‘ta keskin variant. Matnda “not entirely convinced” bo‘lsa, “completely opposed” noto‘g‘ri. Ikkinchi: to‘g‘ri, lekin savolga javob bermaydigan gap. Uchinchi: muallif pozitsiyasining aksi, ko‘pincha u keltirgan boshqa odamning fikri. To‘rtinchi: matndagi so‘zlarni takrorlaydigan, lekin ma’nosi boshqa variant.
scenes.say: Too extreme, true but beside the point, the opposite view, or simply borrowed words. Those are the four traps.
scenes.say_uz: O‘ta keskin, to‘g‘ri lekin chetda, qarama-qarshi fikr yoki shunchaki olingan so‘zlar. Mana shu to‘rt tuzoq.

scenes.title: So‘z mos keldi, demak to‘g‘ri
board: ✗ The option repeats “innovation”, so it is right.
✓ Paraphrase is usually the right answer.
scenes.say_native: Bizning o‘quvchilarda eng ko‘p uchraydigan xato: matndagi so‘z variantda ham bo‘lsa, uni darhol tanlash. Aslida to‘g‘ri javob deyarli har doim parafraz, ya’ni boshqa so‘zlar bilan aytilgan ma’no. Matndan so‘zma-so‘z olingan variant ko‘pincha tuzoq. Shuning uchun ma’noni solishtiring, so‘zlarni emas. Keyingi darslarda parafrazni alohida o‘rganamiz, bu ko‘nikma u yerda ham kerak bo‘ladi.
scenes.say: If an option repeats a striking word from the text, be suspicious. Compare meanings, not vocabulary.
scenes.say_uz: Variant matndagi yorqin so‘zni takrorlasa, shubha qiling. So‘zlarni emas, ma’nolarni solishtiring.

scenes.title: Mashq: xulosa savoli
board: Text: “The festival, now in its tenth year, has never lacked ambition. Whether it has ever had a coherent programme is another matter.”
The writer implies the festival is:
A unambitious  B poorly organised in content
C too old  D extremely popular
scenes.say_native: Qisqa matnni o‘qing. Muallif festival haqida nimaga ishora qilyapti? Avval o‘z so‘zingiz bilan javob bering, keyin to‘rt variantdan birini tanlang. Qaysi variant aksi, qaysi biri so‘z tuzog‘i, qaysi biri matnda umuman yo‘q, buni ham aniqlang. To‘rt qadamni eslang.
scenes.say: The festival has never lacked ambition. Whether it has ever had a coherent programme is another matter. What does the writer imply?
scenes.say_uz: Festival hech qachon ambitsiyadan mahrum bo‘lmagan. U qachondir izchil dasturga ega bo‘lganmi, bu boshqa masala. Muallif nimaga ishora qiladi?

scenes.title: Javob: B
board: C ✗ not implied · D ✗ not stated
scenes.say_native: To‘g‘ri javob B. “Whether it has ever had a coherent programme is another matter” degan ibora muallif dastur izchil emasligiga ishora qilishini ko‘rsatadi, lekin buni ochiq aytmaydi. A variant aksi, chunki ambitsiya maqtalgan. C variantda “tenth year” so‘zi bor, bu so‘z tuzog‘i, muallif festival eskirgan demaydi. D esa matnda umuman yo‘q.
scenes.say: B is correct. Another matter is a polite way of saying no.
scenes.say_uz: B to‘g‘ri. Another matter “yo‘q” deyishning xushmuomala usuli.

scenes.title: Tinglash 1: maqola muhokamasi
board: Listen: two colleagues discuss an opinion column
Focus: the columnist's attitude and purpose
scenes.say_native: Endi birinchi tinglash. Ikki hamkasb gazetadagi sharh maqolasini muhokama qilmoqda. Ular maqoladan iqtiboslar keltiradi. Diqqat qiling: sharhlovchi shahar markazidagi yangi velosiped yo‘laklariga qanday munosabatda? Uning maqsadi nima? Va ikki hamkasb maqolani bir xil tushunadimi?
scenes.say: Ben: Did you read Hart's column on the cycle lanes? Sara: I did. She calls them a bold experiment, then spends six paragraphs on the so-called consultation. Ben: I thought she was broadly in favour. Sara: Read it again. Admittedly, the air is cleaner, she says, but the shops are emptying. And she ends by saying the council has, once again, listened carefully to itself. Ben: Ah. So that's not praise. Sara: Not remotely. She wants the scheme reviewed.
scenes.say_uz: Ben: Hartning velosiped yo‘laklari haqidagi sharhini o‘qidingmi? Sara: O‘qidim. U ularni dadil tajriba deydi, keyin olti xatboshini go‘yoki maslahatlashuvga bag‘ishlaydi. Ben: Men u umuman tarafdor deb o‘ylagandim. Sara: Qayta o‘qi. To‘g‘ri, havo tozaroq, deydi u, lekin do‘konlar bo‘shab qolmoqda. Va oxirida kengash yana bir bor o‘zini diqqat bilan tingladi, deydi. Ben: Hmm. Demak bu maqtov emas. Sara: Umuman emas. U sxemani qayta ko‘rib chiqishni xohlaydi.

scenes.title: Savollar: 1-tinglash
board: 1 What is the columnist's attitude to the consultation?
3 What is the purpose of the column?
scenes.say_native: Dialog bo‘yicha to‘rtta savol. Sharhlovchi maslahatlashuvga qanday qaraydi? Qaysi ibora kinoyali? Maqolaning maqsadi nima? Va nima uchun Ben maqolani noto‘g‘ri tushundi? Har bir javob uchun dialogdan bitta so‘z yoki iborani eslang. Pauza qiling, javob yozing.
scenes.say: Four questions. What is the columnist's attitude to the consultation? Which phrase is ironic? What is the column's purpose? And why did Ben misread it? Pause now.
scenes.say_uz: To‘rtta savol. Sharhlovchi maslahatlashuvga qanday qaraydi? Qaysi ibora kinoyali? Maqolaning maqsadi nima? Va nima uchun Ben uni noto‘g‘ri tushundi? Hozir pauza qiling.

scenes.title: Javoblar: 1-tinglash
board: 3 to criticise and call for a review
4 he took “bold experiment” at face value
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: shubha bilan, chunki “so-called consultation” degan ibora bor. Ikkinchi: “the council has listened carefully to itself”, ya’ni kengash hech kimni tinglamagan. Uchinchi: maqsad tanqid qilish va sxemani qayta ko‘rib chiqishga chaqirish. To‘rtinchi: Ben faqat boshidagi “bold experiment” iborasini o‘qib, keyingi admittedly va but ni e’tiborsiz qoldirgan. Bu biz o‘rgangan xato.
scenes.say: Sceptical, because of so-called. The irony: the council listened carefully to itself. The purpose: to call for a review.
scenes.say_uz: Shubhali, chunki so-called bor. Kinoya: kengash o‘zini diqqat bilan tingladi. Maqsad: qayta ko‘rib chiqishga chaqirish.

scenes.title: Tinglash 2: kitob taqrizi
board: Listen: a radio presenter reads from a book review
Focus: fact vs opinion, hedges, final verdict
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi tinglash. Radio boshlovchisi yangi tarix kitobi haqidagi taqrizdan parcha o‘qiydi. Bu safar fakt va fikrni ajrating, ehtiyotkorlik iboralarini toping va taqrizchining yakuniy hukmi nima ekanini aniqlang. Matn muvozanatli ko‘rinadi, lekin munosabat nozik.
scenes.say: Presenter: Here's how the review opens. Nadia Rahman's new history of the Silk Road runs to six hundred pages and draws on archives in four languages. It is, at times, a genuinely absorbing read. Rahman is at her best on trade; on religion she is noticeably thinner. Some readers may find the final chapters rushed, and the claim that Samarkand was the centre of the medieval world is asserted rather than argued. Still, this is a book that deserves a wide audience.
scenes.say_uz: Boshlovchi: Taqriz shunday boshlanadi. Nadia Rahmanning Ipak yo‘li haqidagi yangi tarix kitobi olti yuz sahifadan iborat va to‘rt tildagi arxivlarga tayanadi. U ba’zan chinakam maroqli o‘qiladi. Rahman savdo haqida eng kuchli, din mavzusida esa sezilarli darajada sayozroq. Ba’zi o‘quvchilar so‘nggi boblarni shoshilinch deb topishi mumkin, Samarqand o‘rta asrlar dunyosining markazi bo‘lgan degan da’vo esa asoslanmagan, shunchaki ta’kidlangan. Baribir, bu keng auditoriyaga loyiq kitob.

scenes.title: Savollar: 2-tinglash
board: 1 Name two facts in the review.
3 What does “asserted rather than argued” imply?
4 Overall verdict: hostile, positive with reservations, or neutral?
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta savol. Taqrizdan ikkita faktni ayting. Bitta ehtiyotkorlik iborasini toping. “Asserted rather than argued” nimaga ishora qiladi? Va umumiy hukm qanday: dushmanona, eslatmalar bilan ijobiy yoki neytral? Oxirgi gapga alohida e’tibor bering. Pauza qiling.
scenes.say: Name two facts. Find one hedge. What does asserted rather than argued imply? And is the overall verdict hostile, positive with reservations, or neutral? Pause now.
scenes.say_uz: Ikkita faktni ayting. Bitta hedge toping. Asserted rather than argued nimaga ishora qiladi? Umumiy hukm dushmanona, eslatmalar bilan ijobiy yoki neytralmi? Hozir pauza qiling.

scenes.title: Javoblar: 2-tinglash
scenes.say_native: Faktlar: olti yuz sahifa va to‘rt tildagi arxivlar, bularni tekshirish mumkin. Hedge: “at times” va “some readers may find”. “Asserted rather than argued” degani muallif da’voni dalilsiz aytgan, bu yumshoq, lekin jiddiy tanqid. Yakuniy hukm eslatmalar bilan ijobiy: “Still” so‘zi kamchiliklardan keyin asosiy bahoga qaytadi, “deserves a wide audience” esa tavsiya.
scenes.say: Facts: six hundred pages, four languages. Hedges: at times, may find. The verdict: positive, with reservations.
scenes.say_uz: Faktlar: olti yuz sahifa, to‘rt til. Hedge: at times, may find. Hukm: eslatmalar bilan ijobiy.

scenes.title: Ovozda ohang: urg‘u va intonatsiya
board: Fall-rise on concession: Admittedly ↘↗, it's cheap...

examples.t: Well, that went well.

scenes.say_native: Og‘zaki nutqda munosabat intonatsiya orqali ham beriladi. Samimiy “Oh, brilliant!” baland boshlanadi va yorqin tushadi. Kinoyali “Oh, brilliant” esa past, tekis va sekin aytiladi. Tan olishda, masalan “Admittedly, it’s cheap”, admittedly so‘zida tushib-ko‘tariluvchi ohang bo‘ladi va tinglovchi “but” kelishini sezadi. Bu ko‘nikma keyingi tinglash darsida ham juda kerak bo‘ladi.
scenes.say: Sincere: Oh, brilliant! Ironic: Oh. Brilliant. And a concession: Admittedly, it's cheap...
scenes.say_uz: Samimiy: Voy, ajoyib! Kinoyali: Ha. Ajoyib. Va tan olish: To‘g‘ri, arzon...

scenes.title: Mashq: ikki xil ohangda ayting
board: Say each line twice: sincere, then ironic
2 That was a really useful meeting.
scenes.say_native: Har bir gapni ikki marta ovoz chiqarib ayting: avval samimiy, keyin kinoyali. Samimiy variantda ovozingiz baland va jonli bo‘lsin, kinoyalida esa past, tekis va sekin. Agar imkon bo‘lsa, o‘zingizni telefonga yozib oling va ikki variant farqini tinglang.
scenes.say: Say each line twice, first sincerely, then ironically. What a lovely surprise. That was a really useful meeting. Pause and try it now.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir satrni ikki marta ayting, avval samimiy, keyin kinoyali. Qanday yoqimli kutilmagan sovg‘a. Bu juda foydali yig‘ilish bo‘ldi. Pauza qilib, hozir sinab ko‘ring.

scenes.title: Namuna: ikki ohang
board: Sincere: wide pitch range, stress on lovely / useful
Ironic: narrow range, slow, stress on really
scenes.say_native: Namunani tinglang va o‘zingiznikini solishtiring. Samimiy variantda ovoz diapazoni keng, urg‘u lovely va useful so‘zlariga tushadi. Kinoyali variantda ovoz tor diapazonda, sekin, urg‘u ko‘pincha really so‘zida cho‘ziladi. Yozma matnda esa ovoz yo‘q, shuning uchun kinoyani faqat kontekst ko‘rsatadi: maqtov vaziyatga mos kelmasa, bu signal.
scenes.say: Sincere: What a lovely surprise! Ironic: What a lovely surprise. That was a really... useful meeting.
scenes.say_uz: Samimiy: Qanday yoqimli kutilmagan sovg‘a! Kinoyali: Qanday yoqimli kutilmagan sovg‘a. Bu juda... foydali yig‘ilish bo‘ldi.

scenes.title: Yakuniy vazifa: tahlil yozing
board: Text: “The airline’s new “premium economy” offers, we are told, more legroom. Passengers may wish to bring a ruler.”
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy vazifa. Doskadagi qisqa parchani o‘qing va uch gapdan iborat tahlil yozing. Birinchi gap: muallifning maqsadi. Ikkinchi gap: munosabati va uni isbotlaydigan ikkita so‘z yoki ibora. Uchinchi gap: muallif qaysi usuldan foydalangan, masalan kinoya yoki qo‘shtirnoq. Pauza qilib, yozing.
scenes.say: Read the extract and write a three-sentence analysis: the writer's purpose, their attitude with two pieces of evidence, and the technique they use. Pause and write.
scenes.say_uz: Parchani o‘qing va uch gaplik tahlil yozing: muallifning maqsadi, munosabati va ikkita dalil, hamda u qo‘llagan usul. Pauza qilib, yozing.

scenes.title: Namunaviy tahlil
board: The writer aims to mock the airline's marketing.
The tone is sceptical: scare quotes, “we are told”.
The ruler joke uses irony to imply little extra space.
scenes.say_native: Namunaviy javob. Birinchi: muallif aviakompaniya reklamasini masxara qilishni maqsad qilgan. Ikkinchi: ohang shubhali, buni “premium economy” atrofidagi qo‘shtirnoq va “we are told” iborasi ko‘rsatadi, ya’ni muallif bu da’voni o‘z zimmasiga olmaydi. Uchinchi: chizg‘ich haqidagi hazil kinoya, u qo‘shimcha joy shunchalik kamki, uni o‘lchash kerak bo‘lishiga ishora qiladi. Sizning javobingizda ham uch qism bormi?
scenes.say: The writer aims to mock the airline's marketing. The tone is sceptical. The ruler joke is ironic.
scenes.say_uz: Muallif aviakompaniya reklamasini masxara qilmoqchi. Ohang shubhali. Chizg‘ich haqidagi hazil kinoyali.

scenes.title: Darsning xulosasi
board: Stance: adverbs, hedges, boosters, reporting verbs
scenes.say_native: Xulosa. Birinchi: ohang so‘z tanlovida, kinoyada va yumshoq ifodada yashiringan, uni mavzu bilan aralashtirmang. Ikkinchi: pozitsiya belgilari, ya’ni admittedly, ostensibly, hedge va boosterlar, hamda claims yoki demonstrates kabi fe’llar. Uchinchi: fakt tekshiriladi, fikr baholaydi, raqamlarning ramkasi ham pozitsiya. To‘rtinchi: xulosa savollarida joyni toping, taxmin qiling va chiqarib tashlang.
scenes.say: Tone lives in word choice. Stance lives in adverbs, hedges and verbs. Facts can be checked. Inferences need evidence.
scenes.say_uz: Ohang so‘z tanlovida. Pozitsiya ravishlar, hedge va fe’llarda. Faktni tekshirish mumkin. Xulosa dalil talab qiladi.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi va keyingi dars
board: Homework: Analyse the attitude of an opinion article
1 fact vs 1 opinion · 1 inference with evidence
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: ingliz tilidagi bitta sharh maqolasini tanlang, masalan gazetaning opinion bo‘limidan, va uning munosabatini tahlil qiling. Mezon: maqsad va munosabatni aniq sifat bilan nomlang, kamida beshta pozitsiya belgisini iqtibos qiling, bitta faktni va bitta fikrni ajrating va matndan dalil bilan bitta xulosa chiqaring. Keyingi darsda tez nutq va turli aksentlarni tushunishni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Your homework: analyse the attitude of an opinion article, quoting at least five stance markers. Next time: fast speech and accents.
scenes.say_uz: Uy vazifangiz: sharh maqolasining munosabatini tahlil qiling, kamida beshta pozitsiya belgisini iqtibos qiling. Keyingi dars: tez nutq va aksentlar.

homework_uz: Ingliz tilidagi bitta sharh (opinion) maqolasini tanlang va muallif munosabatini tahlil qiling. Mezon: maqsad va ohangni aniq sifat bilan nomlang, kamida beshta pozitsiya belgisini (ravish, hedge, iqtibos fe’li, so-called kabi) iqtibos qiling, bitta fakt va bitta fikrni ajrating, matndan dalil bilan bitta xulosa chiqaring. Hajmi 150–200 so‘z.

quiz.q: “The plan is not without its problems.” The writer means the plan has:
quiz.why_uz: Litotes: inkorni inkor qilish. Not without its problems = muammolar ko‘p.

quiz.q: Which reporting verb shows the writer doubts the claim?
quiz.why_uz: Alleges masofa saqlaydi va shubha bildiradi; qolganlari rozilik.

quiz.q: “Admittedly, the hotel is central.” What usually comes next?
quiz.why_uz: Admittedly tan olishni bildiradi, asl fikr esa odatda but bilan keladi.

quiz.q: Which sentence is a pure fact?
options: The stadium is a monument to bad taste.
quiz.why_uz: Sig‘imni tekshirish mumkin; qolganlarida baho yoki modal bor.

quiz.q: “The scheme is ostensibly about road safety.” The writer suggests:
options: the real purpose may be different
quiz.why_uz: Ostensibly = go‘yoki: rasmiy sabab haqiqiy sababga mos kelmasligi mumkin.

quiz.q: Choose the correct verb: From the evidence, the reader can ___ that the author disapproves.
quiz.why_uz: O‘quvchi infer qiladi, muallif imply qiladi.

quiz.q: Which word best describes a writer who weighs both sides calmly?
“Only 30% of voters turned out.” The word only shows that the writer thinks the figure is:
In an inference question, an option that repeats exact words from the text is often:
quiz.why_uz: To‘g‘ri javob odatda parafraz; so‘zma-so‘z mos kelish ko‘pincha tuzoq.

quiz.q: “The so-called reform changed nothing.” The writer's attitude is:
quiz.why_uz: So-called muallif bu nomga rozi emasligini ko‘rsatadi: shubha.
